segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making the time, Dana. I have you at 44 paid users for the calibration scheduling module, plus two finance folks who only need invoice and certificate viewing. Is that still right?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That’s right. Thirty-eight field techs, six coordinators, and then finance just wants read-only access so they can pull certs when customers ask.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Perfect. On the standard annual plan, the 44 paid seats are $68 per user per month. The read-only users are included. So the subscription is $35,904 for the year, and implementation is a one-time $4,800.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. I need the invoice to match those two lines exactly, subscription and implementation. Our AP team gets picky if it’s bundled together.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, no problem. It’ll show as two separate line items, total of $40,704, net 30. Term would run September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. For timing, we want the system live for the October 5 calibration cycle. Is that realistic if we sign by next Friday, August 14?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. If we’re signed by August 14, kickoff can be the week of August 24, your equipment import would be due September 4, and training would land September 23 and 24. That gives you a little buffer before October 5.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. One other thing: if we add, say, five technicians in January, are they at the same $68 rate?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: They are. Additional paid seats are prorated at the same $68 per user per month through August 31, 2027. If you need to reduce seats, we’d true that down at renewal.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Send me the order form with those dates and the net 30 terms, and I’ll route it with the PO request.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send it over today, and I’ll include the implementation schedule in the same note so your ops lead can review it.
